Unfortunately, the list I'm working off of is slightly different from the ones that you have in front of you, but I will identify the exhibits for which there is no objection, and those would be Prosecutor's Exhibits 65 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, I'm sorry to interrupt you. You don't think it is possible to use this list that has been submitted to the Chamber? If not, we will just take notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You can use this list, Mr. President. I just have a list that's not in sync, in terms of numerical sequence, with the list that's before you. But I can give you the exhibit number and then give you time to turn to the list, that item, and then you can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I just wanted to know whether we're talking about the same things, otherwise we would be talking at cross-purposes. So we can use the list that you have given us. Please continue, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Prosecutor's Exhibit 65, there is no objection, Prosecutor's Exhibit 221, Prosecutor's Exhibit 399. The Prosecution withdraws Exhibit 790. Prosecutor's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I don't see 790 on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I have been informed that has been removed from the list, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Prosecutor's Exhibit 136, Prosecutor's Exhibit 228. 228, Your Honours, is being offered under seal, as is 228A bis, 228B bis and 228C bis. Prosecutor's Exhibit 359/A bis also is being offered under seal. Prosecutor's Exhibit 399/A bis and B bis, Prosecutor's Exhibit 69 bis, Prosecutor's Exhibit 823/A bis, Prosecutor's Exhibit 830/A bis, Prosecutor's Exhibit 222/A, and 223/A, 228C bis, and that exhibit is being offered under seal. Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry once again to interrupt you. I cannot see 222C bis [In English] 228C bis. [Interpretation] You have already mentioned this one, and in your list I cannot see "under seal" remark next to that exhibit. [In English] It's a revised French translation of full interview?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. That should be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Okay. But we have not here. Good. Go on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. Prosecutor's Exhibit 32C bis, Prosecutor's Exhibit 127, Prosecutor's Exhibit 792. One additional comment on one additional exhibit is Prosecutor's Exhibit 882. It was admitted, I believe it was yesterday, or this week, on the condition that the Prosecutor show to the Defence the original notebook. Your Honours, we have met with Defence counsel and we have shown them the original notebook, and they're satisfied and can confirm that fact. Those are the exhibits --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: We only have 792A and B on my list. You mentioned 792. Is that the same as 792A and B?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The remaining exhibits are contested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but the Exhibit 882 is not included in the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: As I said, Your Honour, it's already been admitted. Your Honour posed a condition on that that we show to the Defence the copy of the notebook. We have done that to satisfy that condition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Before I give the floor to Mr. Visnjic, I think that this list needs to be admitted as an exhibit so that we can work on the basis of that, Mr. Harmon. What do you think? Because -- but maybe not. Maybe it's not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This document was prepared as an aid, not as an exhibit, and I'm not sure we're confident enough in the details in it to have it as an exhibit, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. No. Really, it's not necessary. Mr. Visnjic, can you confirm that all the exhibits that Mr. Harmon has just mentioned have not been objected to by the Defence? Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Have you finished, Mr. Visnjic? Mr. Harmon, I see you are on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: One exhibit should be also included as an exhibit that is for admission. It's Exhibit 28, which is a booklet with approximately 13 or 15 tabs with photographs of individuals, and we are moving for the admission of that particular document but we are moving to withdraw one of the tabbed sections in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe I could be of assistance, Mr. President. It is number 15, 28/15.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's correct, it is the photograph in that exhibit 28 that purports to be Colonel Beara. It is the photograph that's marked on the back 28/15, and so we are moving to withdraw that part of Exhibit 28 and move the remaining part of the exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I shall try to be brief, and if it is not clear enough for the record, will try again, namely the group of Defence exhibits from 27 through to 71 were disputed. With the Prosecution, we have reached agreement that all these documents with the exception of document 38 have been made undisputed. Similarly, there was also an objection to Exhibit D74, and I understand from the Prosecution that that exhibit, too, is not being challenged now. With respect to Exhibit D165, we have given the Prosecution certain information about the source, that is how the Defence gained possession of that document, and the response we received was that they were satisfied with that information on condition that we present them here for the record for which purpose I would request that we briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let us go briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I should also like to notify the Trial Chamber that the Defence has supplied sufficient number of copies of the expert report of Mr. Stankovic and Mr. Simic, and they are Exhibits D171 and D172 in both versions, that is in both the Serbian and the English version. That would be all, Mr. President, with respect to the agreement reached with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Mr. Visnjic, does that mean that you are asking these two reports to be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have already made such a request. The only thing that we still had to do was provide sufficient copies for the members of the Trial Chamber and the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, with respect to these two reports, have you any remarks to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In respect of D171 and D172, the two reports, we have no objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Visnjic. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: May we have a moment to confer, just between us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there is another Defence exhibit outstanding that we left out, and that is 53 and 46, which were withdrawn earlier on. I just wish to confirm this for the record. D53 and D46 are being withdrawn by the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that all, Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is all, Mr. President, regarding the agreements that we have reached with the Prosecution. Of course there is the disputed part that remains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's see now, perhaps we can already rule on the following: The Exhibit 790 of the Prosecution and Exhibits 53 and 46 of the Defence have been withdrawn by the parties concerned. I have already made a checklist with the registrar, and we have agreed to admit all the documents which were mentioned and noted as not being in dispute and with no objections being made by either party. So to avoid repeating all the exhibits - I think the transcript is clear - so that is our general ruling. We also need to add to the withdrawn exhibits the Prosecution Exhibit 28/15, tab 15. And I think that's all for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I just clarify one thing. Exhibit 28, it should be 28/15 and not tab 15, because they're multiple photographs in a tab, and if you eliminate tab 15, you'll be withdrawing the wrong photograph. It's a confusing exhibit, but on the back of each photograph there is a number, and it is the photograph 1, the section with Colonel Beara, and the photograph that purports to be Colonel Beara has on its back 28/15, and it is that particular exhibit we're moving to withdraw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much, Mr. Harmon, for this clarification, so we will note the exhibits along the lines you have just explained. I think that now we need to ask the parties whether all the other exhibits, is the Chamber going to take them and rule on their admission or do you have any other suggestions to make to the Chamber? In other words, you have done what you could with respect to all the exhibits, and it is up to the Chamber to do the rest, or do you have any other possibilities in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Obviously, I have some additional comments on certain of these exhibits, and then it's up to the Chamber to make decisions on these. I haven't addressed any of those comments as to those particular exhibits at this point because I was waiting until the opportunity arose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think perhaps that the time has come, because of time constraints, so you can make those comments. Or, if you prefer, you could do so in writing, and we will make our ruling in writing too. Maybe that's another possibility, for practical reasons, in view of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm at your disposal, Mr. President. We're at the end of the case. We have some very important exhibits here that I think have to be discussed with the Chamber. The reasons set forth why we believe they are admissible and why my colleagues think they are objectionable should be put on the record in some form, and it's incumbent on us to offer these into evidence so the Court can make a ruling. I say that because there are yet some additional issues that are still before this Court that need to be addressed before we conclude these proceedings. For example, in respect of Prosecution Exhibit 833, the Defence has filed a motion. We haven't had an opportunity to be heard on our views on our particular motion. We simply haven't had time to prepare a written answer. I'm prepared to address those remarks orally or I'm prepared to submit our remarks in writing, depending on what the Chamber wishes to do. In addition, Mr. President, there was a protected witness, Witness II. There are certain factors about the timing of that witness which may be in dispute at some point, and I think it's important and I would like the opportunity to insert into the record the factors that relate to the timing of the Prosecution's discovery of that evidence that I think have a bearing on other objections that have been made in this case and have a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. bearing on other exhibits that also have been tendered by us. Lastly, Mr. President, I would need to insert into the record just a fact about some revised translations and some language service efforts to clarify at least some of the terminology in at least two exhibits. One was at the request of Judge Riad. There has been a clarification by the Language Service Section. So there's a number of issues that we still need to address before we conclude this, and if we have only a matter of a few minutes, I don't think it's sufficient time to do that, and I'm at your disposal how you would like us to do that. But at the end of this trial, I want to ensure that Prosecutor's exhibits that have been tendered, one, are formally tendered; and two, the reasons why we believe they are relevant. And we can anticipate the Defence objections, why we think the Defence objections are ill-founded, we would like that inserted into the record as well. So I'm at your disposal, Mr. President, how you would like to address that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, roughly how many, just roughly, how many exhibits are disputed?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'd say, Judge Wald --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Just rough.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- every exhibit that we offered in rebuttal is disputed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Yes. I -- that's a kind of one big issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So there are all of those exhibits. I don't have the number, but I would say probably 25 exhibits are disputed. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I can be more precise. If you give me a minute, I can count them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you give me a few minutes now. I wish to confer with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber has a proposition to make to the parties. I think there are several interests involved here. One is to review the whole documentation, and especially and in particular, the exhibits which are in dispute. As Mr. Harmon has said, we need to hear the arguments of the parties: Why, what are the points of view of each party. Therefore, I think that in order to organise each exhibit and the arguments of the parties, one could give the parties the opportunity to do so in writing. That is a way for each of the parties to review the evidence and organise itself. After that, we would come to the courtroom for a summary presentation of the reasons that were already conveyed to the Chamber. In that way, we will all have the material and all the information we need. Perhaps that would be a better organised manner and a fairer one to address the issue, and also an efficient one in terms of the ruling. Do you agree? Also, we have to see when the parties are available to come to the courtroom, knowing that next week we are sitting only for two working days because there is the plenary on Thursday, and after that -- Judge Wald is telling me that we have a holiday. I don't think that's the right word, but never mind. What do you think about it, Mr. Harmon and, after that, Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We have a trial brief to prepare and we need to know, obviously, when evidence is in and when evidence is out to prepare this adequately. So certainly our interests are to get resolution as soon as possible on these issues. If it's a question of preparing something in writing, we have no objection to that. I think we could get through this in 20 minutes. I think the objections of the Defence are uniform. They could -- but either way, we are prepared to proceed as long as we can get a quick resolution of the issues so we could prepare our trial brief which, as you know, is a project that is ongoing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How about Wednesday for you, Mr. Harmon? Wednesday afternoon at the end of the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Wednesday is fine. I was planning to go fishing, but Wednesday is fine, Mr. President. I will be here and we can do that on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you are going to fish for exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We will do that, Mr. President. Wednesday afternoon is fine. Does Your Honour have a suggestion as to when you'd like something in writing or is that the date for the written submission?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, as you know, there is a slight delay with the interpretation so I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So fine. I think that we have reached a decision. I think it is better for each party, we will come here on Wednesday, perhaps around 4.00, and the parties can bring, in writing, their arguments as concisely as possible because with respect to the exhibits, because with regard to those presented during the rebuttal and rejoinder, we had a lot of discussion. It is always a good idea to have concise arguments and this also applies to the other disputed exhibits. So Wednesday around 4.00. I apologise for upsetting your fishing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The fish don't -- thank you. They never get caught anyway, Mr. President. Mr. President, I'm happy to abide by that schedule. That, again, leaves the issue of the argument on the motion for a continuance, that will also be the same date, I take it. And if I could either now or on that date put in the record the facts I'd like to about Witness II. If I could reserve that until Wednesday as well, I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. All the questions that are outstanding, we need to finish with them on Wednesday, not only the exhibit but all the other matters. What about the Defence? Are you agreeable with this procedure? You're not going fishing, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, but my colleague Mr. Petrusic will not be here next week, so if the Trial Chamber does not mind, we would like to ask your leave for me alone to be present for that hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As you know, we appreciate very much the presence of Mr. Petrusic, but it is up to you to organise yourselves. The courtroom is happy to have you present, but if you agree on that procedure, we have no problem with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, then. I think that we have come to a way out of this situation. So we will meet again on Wednesday at 4.00 to address the remaining issues. So have a good weekend and success in your work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
